question: Which video recordings captured the moment of the shooting on 2025-09-10, and which have been released publicly?
known: The host refers to footage of the shooting without naming its source (C-56). The record in this pack does not inventory the shooting videos.
settle: An evidence list of all seized and public videos of the tent area 12:20-12:25, with original files, sources and capture metadata.

question: Did Charlie Kirk's public or private position on Israel and its supporters change in 2024-2025 before his death, and what do his statements, authenticated messages (including the September 9 group chat) and accounts of those around him show?
known: The host says Kirk was undergoing a change of heart, had many doubts known to his inner circle, wavered in his own words, said he did not want the money, and was done with the pro-Israel cause, and that she, Kelly and Carlson described this accurately from their own talks with him (C-60, C-62, C-100, C-275, C-1131, C-1142, C-1316, C-1556, C-2164, C-2220, C-2221, C-2325, C-2650, C-3989, C-3453, C-6464, C-6568, C-6501, C-6906, C-6909, C-6966, C-7080, C-7199, C-7275, C-7335, C-8846, C-8849, C-8850, C-9605, C-9674, C-14223); a clip shows Kirk saying pro-Israel behaviour was pushing people like him away (C-260), and a viewer says he abandoned the cause the day before (C-14272). Kent says the public texts show Kirk under pressure from pro-Israel donors (C-7251). Josh Hammer says Kirk never flinched or blinked on Israel (C-1512); the host says participants who said so had argued with him the night before (C-7280, C-7343), that Erika has not acknowledged his shift (C-2224, C-6451), and suspects his last day involved arguments over it (C-6544). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Kirk's dated public statements and broadcasts in 2024-2025, including the July 2025 student session; the authenticated group-chat export and private messages, including September 9; on-record accounts from Carlson, Kelly, Hammer, chat participants, donors and Erika Kirk.

question: When did Benjamin Netanyahu first post about the shooting, relative to other world leaders and to TPUSA's own first statements?
known: The host says Netanyahu was posting first and following events minute by minute (C-63). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Archived timestamps of Netanyahu's posts on 2025-09-10 alongside those of other leaders and TPUSA accounts.

question: Did Erika Kirk mention Benjamin Netanyahu or Israel in her public remarks after the assassination?
known: The host says she does not recall any such mention (C-64). The record says nothing yet.
settle: The full transcript and video of Erika Kirk's post-assassination remarks.

question: Did Netanyahu speak with Kirk in the weeks before the shooting and invite him to Israel, how was it communicated, and how did Kirk respond?
known: Netanyahu says in clips that he called Kirk a few weeks before and invited him to Israel (C-68, C-444); the host places the invitation about two weeks before Kirk's death and says Kirk declined, which Netanyahu omits (C-89, C-252, C-273, C-450, C-1547, C-1548), while also saying Kirk said he would love to go (C-451). No record yet.
settle: Call logs or scheduling records from the Prime Minister's office and TPUSA, Kirk's messages about the call, and on-record accounts from his staff.

question: Did donors or pro-Israel figures pressure Charlie Kirk and TPUSA in 2023-2025 over Israel or over whom he hosted and associated with (such as Tucker Carlson, Candace Owens or Dave Smith), including by threatening or withdrawing funds, and who were they?
known: The host says Kirk was under donor pressure from October 7, 2023 (C-11289, C-11370, C-11436) and that donors threatened to withdraw money and dictated speakers, with pressure peaking before the shooting (C-74, C-75, C-96, C-97, C-233, C-467, C-471, C-474, C-475). She says Kirk felt 'morally blackmailed', including over the Hamptons and his friendship with her, and planned to bring her back (C-713, C-714, C-717, C-718, C-758); that donors demanded he bar her from AmFest and denounce her, that he refused, and that she will name the donor who yelled at him (C-2791, C-2890, C-3130, C-3136, C-3144). She names Seth Dillon, Josh Hammer and Bob Shillman as angry after Carlson's 2025-07-11 speech, says a donor confronted Kirk backstage, that Shillman withdrew money, that Jewish and Christian Zionist donors threatened him financially, that pro-Israel actors pulled money and Shapiro used donor connections against him, and that the pressure made Kirk ill (C-1136, C-1517, C-1536, C-2050, C-2127, C-2128, C-2187, C-2213, C-2221, C-2352, C-2657, C-4957, C-5320, C-5525, C-5526, C-6905, C-6967, C-7099); Megyn Kelly is said to have described the pressure (C-1561, C-2227). She says Bowyer told her TPUSA will always be pro-Israel (C-2126), that Erika Kirk faces the same pressure (C-2061), that Kirk's death served Netanyahu's war aims (C-5010), and that those close to Kirk will not name the donors (C-1065). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Dated donor and staff correspondence with Kirk from late 2023 through 2025-09-10; TPUSA donor records and 990s before and after the July 2025 Student Action Summit; Hammer's and Dillon's posts of July 11-13; AmFest speaker decisions; on-record accounts from those named, Kelly, Carlson and TPUSA staff.

question: Did TPUSA see unusual financial, donor or organisational changes in 2025, such as lost funding or the May staffing changes?
known: The host says Kirk alluded to lost funding, donors threatened to pull money, and employees describe May firings and secrecy (C-75, C-233, C-270, C-274, C-476, C-550, C-551, C-556). The record says nothing yet.
settle: TPUSA and TPAction Form 990s and state filings for 2024-2025, payroll and departure records, and employees' on-record accounts.

question: Did Bill Ackman contact Kirk or TPUSA to object to Tucker Carlson's AmFest remarks?
known: The host says Ackman was unhappy and pressed Kirk over them (C-77). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Ackman's messages to Kirk or TPUSA after AmFest 2024, or statements from either party.

question: When was the August 2025 Hamptons gathering with Kirk, who organized, paid for and attended it, was it a TPUSA event, and was Kirk pressed there over Israel?
known: The host dates it to August 5-7, 2025 (earlier episodes gave August 4-5) (C-9671, C-9672). Seth Dillon says in a hearing clip that Kirk called the retreat, about 30 invited people attended, and it was not an intervention, though he disagreed with Kirk on Israel (C-6377, C-6378, C-6379, C-6380, C-6384); Hammer called it cordial and said he brought signed books (C-1684, C-1685). The host, citing attendees, TPUSA employees and her and Max Blumenthal's reporting, says Kirk presented on not being able to criticise Israel and was pressed hard in a heated confrontation led by Dillon and Natasha, that Ackman was upset and paid for influencers, that Kirk called it an intervention and then appeared on Megyn Kelly's show, and that attendees including Hammer and Dillon are lying about it, with the Erickson brothers helping build a false account (C-80, C-235, C-236, C-237, C-238, C-277, C-1351, C-1516, C-1517, C-1546, C-2037, C-2043, C-2050, C-2130, C-2131, C-2507, C-2680, C-2681, C-3453, C-3454, C-6277, C-6366, C-6367, C-6369, C-6390, C-6394, C-6395, C-6399, C-9605). She says Andrew Kolvet was not there (C-581) and attendees will not go on record (C-91, C-92). No record yet.
settle: Invitations and attendee lists (including those sent by Arynne Wexler), the schedule, payment and travel records, photographs, participants' dated statements and on-record accounts, Blumenthal's sourcing, Kirk's messages, and the Megyn Kelly Show episode after the retreat.

question: What did Bill Ackman say publicly and to journalists about the Hamptons gathering, and has he released the messages he said he has?
known: The host reads Ackman's tweet about sharing a meal with Kirk (C-88), says he told Max Blumenthal he had receipts he did not provide (C-81), and characterises his long post and shared texts (C-245, C-249, C-453). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Archived copies of Ackman's posts with timestamps, Blumenthal's correspondence with Ackman, and any texts Ackman published.

question: Was Kirk offered funding at or after the Hamptons gathering, including any funding linked to Netanyahu, and by whom?
known: The host says Kirk was offered a large sum that Netanyahu would have provided (C-85) and that Ackman's response does not address it (C-249). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Messages sent around the gathering that reference an offer, with sender, amount and date, and testimony from attendees.

question: How did Kirk describe the Hamptons gathering, and did he tell anyone he felt pressured, 'morally blackmailed' or subjected to an intervention?
known: The host says Kirk felt blackmailed or that it felt like an intervention and that messages from that time exist (C-87, C-100, C-250); she says Kolvet confirmed Kirk called it an intervention over Israel (C-5696) and that an attendee published a statement using 'morally blackmailed' (C-454). No record yet.
settle: Kirk's dated messages about the gathering, Kolvet's original account, and the attendee's published statement.

question: Was Seth Dillon at the Hamptons gathering, did he pressure Kirk there or elsewhere about criticising Netanyahu, and what do Kirk's messages about Dillon say?
known: The host says Dillon was present and argued aggressively that such criticism would be antisemitic (C-89, C-237, C-11349, C-11350) and that she holds Kirk messages discussing Dillon (C-11284). The record says nothing yet.
settle: The Kirk-Owens messages naming Dillon with metadata; accounts of other Hamptons attendees; Dillon's own account.

question: Did Seth Dillon or donors place calls to TPUSA after the shooting about the host's reporting?
known: The host says Dillon and donors made frantic calls to TPUSA but cites no document (C-90, C-231, C-232). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Call logs or statements from TPUSA staff and the alleged callers.

question: How often were the host and Charlie Kirk in contact after 2017, up to 2025, and what did they discuss, including pressure on him over her and her return to TPUSA events?
known: The host says critics' claims that they had not spoken since 2017 or 2019 are false and that they never stopped being friends (C-1799, C-6257, C-96); she says Kirk discussed Catholicism and Zionism with her over the last year in many texts (C-6568), told her he was pressured over her, and wanted her back on the roster in his final week (C-467, C-472, C-481, C-553). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Authenticated, dated call and message records between the two from 2017 to 2025 with metadata.

question: Does TPUSA hold audio of what Kirk said to Tucker Carlson before Carlson went on stage at AmFest?
known: The host says both were miked and asks TPUSA to release the audio (C-98). The record says nothing yet.
settle: TPUSA's confirmation of whether the microphone recordings exist, and the recordings themselves.

question: Is there any evidence that Israel or another foreign government had a role in planning or carrying out Kirk's assassination?
known: The host first said there was no evidence of Israeli involvement and that she had not alleged it, suspicion arising from perceived cover-up (C-99, C-241, C-520, C-1563, C-1592); she later said she suspects foreign entities and has irrefutable proof of foreign involvement (C-1968, C-2065, C-2066), that France, Israel, the United States and Egypt worked together and Erika was covering for Netanyahu (C-6273, C-6274, C-6281), and that Kirk was the first casualty of the Iran war and 'we all kind of think Israel killed Charlie Kirk', citing no document (C-11731, C-11852). Alex Jones relays unsourced word that Kirk thought Israel would kill him (C-1588). No record yet.
settle: Investigators' findings and discovery on the accused's foreign contacts, finances and communications; charging documents; any findings of the inquiry attributed to Joe Kent or ODNI; the specific documents the host relies on.

question: Who sought to replace Kirk or take control of TPUSA's leadership and direction after his death?
known: The host says she has seen messages from people trying to replace Kirk and describes a 'hostile takeover' (C-109, C-274, C-476). The record says nothing yet.
settle: TPUSA board minutes and leadership appointments after 2025-09-10, and the messages the host says she holds.

question: Was the rifle disassembled after the shot, and in what condition (barrel attached or not) was it recovered?
known: The host and a Michael Savage clip dispute an FBI disassembly account and note a recovery photo with the barrel attached (C-110, C-111, C-120, C-121, C-168). The ruling records texts saying the rifle was left wrapped in a towel in a bush (S-7 07:52:46) but the pack's record does not address disassembly.
settle: The FBI's stated account, the evidence log and photographs of the rifle as found, and a firearms examiner's report.

question: Where, when and by whom was the rifle recovered, had K-9 teams searched that area beforehand, who directed the officers who found it, and how did it get there (was it ever on the roof)?
known: Texts quoted in the record describe leaving the rifle wrapped in a towel in a bush with a squad car parked by it (S-1 p. 8, S-7 07:52:46) (C-137, C-202, C-204); the recovery time, place and finder are not in the cited record. The host says bomb dogs searched the area and missed the gun, which she takes to mean it was planted (C-4549, C-6235, C-7403, C-7674, C-7712, C-7713, C-8365), that federal agents directed rookie officers to it, including Pleasant Grove officer Mitchell Curtis (C-7404, C-11472, C-11473), and relays local law-enforcement sources saying federal agents shifted the stated location (C-7631, C-7632, C-7633). She suggests it was dropped off before or on September 10 (C-8346), says nobody knows how it reached the woods (C-642) and that the gun cannot be connected to Kirk (C-6236), and relays a ground-level account that Robinson dropped the gun at a neighbouring house (C-757). Phil Lyman says he thinks the rifle was in the bushes from the start and never on the roof (C-1023, C-1097).
settle: The evidence recovery log, photographs, incident reports, body-camera footage and testimony of the officers who found it; K-9 deployment logs, handler reports and search maps for 2025-09-10 to 09-11; CAD/dispatch and patrol positioning records; chain of custody; UVU footage of the suspect's route after the shot; trace evidence linking the rifle to the roof.

question: Did anyone besides Tyler Robinson plan, assist, know in advance of, or take part in the shooting?
known: The host repeatedly says Robinson did not act alone: more people were involved, a 'hive', a military or deep-state operation, possibly armed people in the audience, and that she is 99.9 percent certain (C-122, C-191, C-636, C-738, C-754, C-773, C-786, C-816, C-1654, C-1791, C-1792, C-1882, C-1920, C-1958, C-2057, C-2402, C-2403, C-2404, C-2418, C-3674, C-3677, C-4017, C-4024, C-7635, C-11907, C-11940). She and cited sources (including Lance Twiggs's family and a guest) describe George Zinn as a decoy (C-222, C-229, C-430, C-4155), say Charlie was betrayed by people close to him (C-4133), link the timing to other cases (C-4154), mention a Utah person in a local cover-up (C-919), float maroon-shirted look-alikes and note Vance spoke of 'the people who shot Charlie Kirk' (C-8236, C-8282, C-8477), and speculate federal involvement in framing Robinson (C-7644). Carlson says sole action must be proven (C-3922, C-3930); the host says Kash Patel told Megyn Kelly Robinson was the only person involved (C-3745). The record says nothing yet on co-participants.
settle: Charging documents and any superseding charges; FBI and Utah investigative findings on co-conspirators; Robinson's device extractions, Discord, phone, location and financial records (including contacts on 2025-09-09/10); camera footage; trial and hearing evidence.

question: Did the FBI or other authorities state that they were seeking another person in connection with the shooting, and when?
known: The host says the FBI said it was looking for another person (C-112). The record says nothing yet.
settle: The FBI or Utah briefing transcript or release containing the statement, with date.

question: What camera captured the TMZ video of a man walking (reported as 8:07 a.m.), what is its true capture time, how and when did TMZ obtain it and from whom, and does it show Robinson?
known: The host questions the 8:07 time, whether it was a doorbell camera, the occupants of the house and who gave it to TMZ (C-116, C-172, C-408, C-411, C-412, C-414, C-521, C-522); she says TMZ had it by the morning of September 11 and that either the family or federal agents supplied it (C-1168, C-1173). The record says nothing yet.
settle: TMZ's original file with embedded metadata, first publication time and stated source; the camera's location and mounting; the footage's chain of custody; investigators' identification of the person shown.

question: When did Robinson arrive at UVU on 2025-09-10, and where was his Dodge Challenger parked or idling?
known: Governor Cox is quoted as giving an arrival of about 8:29 (C-116); the host says no images of the Challenger have been released (C-395). The ruling and Agent Hull describe Robinson arriving in a maroon shirt and shorts (S-7 07:49:47, S-3 00:47:48) but the pack's record gives no time.
settle: UVU parking and surveillance records for the Challenger and the official timeline of his arrival.

question: Which of Governor Cox's public statements about the suspect, outfits and timeline differ from the charging record?
known: The host says Cox may be the source of miscommunication and cites his 8:29 arrival time (C-116, C-161). The record says nothing yet comparing them.
settle: Transcripts of Cox's briefings set statement by statement against the Information and hearing testimony.

question: What do the rooftop recordings show of the figure on the Losee Center roof: when he arrived, how long he was in position, what he did at the 12:23 shot, and how and when he left?
known: Agent Hull testified the person stayed at the roof edge until the 12:23:28 shot and then moved north (S-3 00:55:27); Sgt. Faumuina said video showed the shooter run southwest to northeast (S-5 04:45:51); the Information describes the low crawl, the dwell and the controlled drop from the roof (S-1 p. 5); Bagley testified dispatch described the rooftop male running to the edge, dropping down, crawling and going prone (S-2 02:34:29), and that he learned from video at the police department that the man jumped off the building (S-2 04:09:47). A witness says the figure dropped onto the roof about 12:20 rather than the federal 12:15, was in position about 20 seconds, and the shot came about 5 seconds after his recording ended (C-10796, C-10799, C-10801, C-10803). The host questions the timing of the run relative to disassembly (C-119, C-120), says the fleeing figure moves too fast to have gone from a firing crouch to a sprint (C-3282), and describes a video of a man laying down before the shot (C-3284). The cited record does not fix the arrival time.
settle: The original rooftop videos and UVU footage of the roof for 12:10-12:30 with embedded timestamps, and the witness clip's metadata; dispatch audio and CAD log; frame-timed expert analysis; witness statements.

question: Where was the fatal shot fired from, and was it fired from the Losee Center roof?
known: Hull and Faumuina testified a person was on the Losee Center roof at the time of the shot (S-3 00:55:27, S-5 04:45:51); the Information alleges a person dropped onto the roof at about 12:15 (S-1 p. 5); Officer Bagley recognised a rifle shot (S-2 01:40:24); and the ruling finds a front-to-back, slightly left-to-right, downward wound path (S-7 07:46:29, 08:16:02), which fixes the direction of entry but not the firing position. Lyman said in hindsight the shot probably came from the roof above him (C-1098), and Neff says the autopsy confirms that direction (C-11528). The host and others dispute it: hunters and military members say another direction (C-512); the host theorises a shot from beneath Kirk or from the audience to his left, says it did not come from behind or the Losee Center, that the rooftop person fired no shot, and favours an exploding microphone (C-607, C-1470, C-1642, C-1660, C-1704, C-7635, C-11575, C-11577); a clip guest argues for a rear shot with a muzzle flash in a window and a figure in a bush (C-906, C-908, C-911, C-913, C-914); O'Neill and the host say witnesses reporting another direction were shut down (C-1463, C-7597); Chaffetz is said to reject the far-shot and Losee theory (C-1648, C-1650).
settle: The medical examiner's wound-trajectory report; ballistic and scene reconstruction against rooftop and seat positions; the rifle, casing and projectile recovery evidence; rooftop camera footage at 12:23; acoustic analysis of the shot.

question: What did George Zinn do and say at the event and afterwards, why was he detained, and was he connected to the shooter or directed, coerced or paid by anyone to act as he did or to claim responsibility?
known: The host calls Zinn a decoy, describes his outburst and shout of 'I did it', his path toward the transport car and the 12:52 custody announcement (C-122, C-155, C-158, C-589, C-13101); a guest theorizes the same (C-4155). She wonders whether he was blackmailed or paid (C-1111, C-1487, C-13102) and says he was featured on Lyman's 2024 campaign site (C-1274). Her sources say he went to Utah Valley Hospital for mild injuries and told people there, including nurses, that he was told to do it or was paid to say it was him (C-2305, C-4157, C-4758, C-7776, C-7777); she also says child-abuse images were found on his phone (C-4757). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Zinn's arrest affidavit, booking report, charging documents and police interviews; dispatch logs and video of his movements after the shot; Utah Valley Hospital intake records and staff statements; financial records; archived 2024 Lyman campaign pages.

question: Where and when were the released stairwell images of the suspect captured, and when were they published?
known: Agent Hull agreed the person-of-interest images released to the press were from the stairwell (S-3 01:53:44), and the Information says photos were published to seek the public's help (S-1 p. 6). Location, time and camera are not given (C-126, C-171, C-178).
settle: The original FBI/Utah release with date and the camera identity and timestamps of the source frames.

question: Did the suspect carry the rifle concealed in his trousers while walking on campus, as surveillance is said to show?
known: The Information alleges an unusual gait with little bending of the right leg 'consistent with a rifle being hidden in his pants' (S-1 p. 5); the host disputes this from the released stills (C-127, C-170, C-171, C-172).
settle: The full surveillance video of the walk and staircase and any gait or forensic analysis produced in discovery.

question: What UVU or other camera footage of the suspect, Tyler Robinson, on or near campus on 2025-09-10 exists, and why has only limited imagery been released?
known: The host says many cameras cover the campus but only grainy images were released (C-128, C-171, C-172, C-394, C-395), and that no clear shot of Robinson and no track of the rooftop shooter has been produced (C-11046, C-10843). No record yet on the camera inventory.
settle: UVU's camera inventory and retained footage, the list of footage seized, Flock and UDOT plate-reader data for Robinson's vehicle, and the authorities' stated reasons for withholding.

question: At what time did Robinson arrive at the Washington County Sheriff's Office on 2025-09-11?
known: The bindover ruling found he arrived about 9:00 PM on September 11 (S-7 07:56:00). The host had heard closer to 7:00 p.m. (C-421).
settle: Already settled by the ruling; sheriff's logs would confirm.

question: What was Robinson wearing on arrival, during the shooting and at surrender, and where did the outfit change take place?
known: The ruling and Hull have him arriving in a maroon shirt and shorts (S-7 07:49:47, S-3 00:47:48) and the Information has a person in dark clothing on the roof (S-1 p. 5); he arrived at the sheriff's office in a maroon shirt and jeans (S-7 07:56:00); texts say he changed outfits by a bush (S-5 02:46:40). The location of the change is not established (C-129, C-139, C-140, C-404, C-405).
settle: Surveillance stills from each stage, booking photographs, and the evidence log for recovered clothing.

question: How did Tyler Robinson come to surrender on 2025-09-11: who learned he had been identified, who contacted whom, what roles did his parents and the family friend (Mike Mitchell) play, was a raid or SWAT action threatened, and did he confess to anyone beforehand?
known: Agents Hull (S-3, 01:51:41) and Davis (S-5, 02:50:14; S-4, 37:00-37:16) testified Robinson went voluntarily to the Washington County Sheriff's Office in St. George with his parents and a family friend; the bindover ruling found the friend picked him up to take him there and quotes a 2025-09-11 Discord message, 'I'm surrendering through a sheriff friend in a few moments' (S-7 07:55:06). The Information says a family friend told him to bring evidence to the sheriff's office (S-1 p. 7), and texts mention a neighbour who was a deputy (S-1 p. 9, S-5 02:49:25). The host and Sheriff Brooksby's clips give competing accounts of the call and what Robinson was told (C-753, C-961, C-962, C-963, C-970, C-972, C-974, C-975, C-977, C-1061); Brooksby described a friend arranging a voluntary surrender (C-7641, C-7642). The host's sources say the friend, Mike Mitchell, told the family to bring him in the easy way or face SWAT, that the parents did not turn him in, and that he went peaceably with his father (C-7627, C-7629, C-7637, C-10609, C-10610, C-11759, C-11831, C-11841, C-11968, C-12641, C-12654). She disputes that the family recognised the grandfather's rifle from a news photo and says Brooksby admitted Robinson was pressed to turn himself in (C-8368, C-8369, C-8371, C-8372); she relays a story that his father turned him in after speaking with a pastor (C-130), notes a clip's account of driving to Orem (C-7397), questions officials' account (C-3999, C-4002), and says no confession or parental turn-in was proven at the hearing (C-10633, C-11441). Whether he confessed and the father's exact words are not settled.
settle: Washington County Sheriff's surrender reports, intake, contact and call logs (including the 8:02 p.m. call); Brooksby's full press-conference recording; statements and testimony of the parents, Mike Mitchell, the deputy and any pastor; interview recordings; the charging documents' surrender narrative and phone records.

question: Did Robinson admit the shooting to friends or acquaintances before his arrest, as Governor Cox described?
known: Governor Cox says acquaintances thought it was a joke until he admitted it (C-132). The record says nothing yet.
settle: The messages in which he allegedly admitted it and the acquaintances' interviews.

question: Which people around Robinson cooperated with investigators, and what did they provide?
known: Cox says everyone around him is cooperating (C-134); Lance Twiggs gave a recorded statement identifying photos of his phone screen (S-5 Exhibit 16, 02:21:58). The host notes little is known about Twiggs (C-214).
settle: Witness lists and interview records from discovery and preliminary hearing testimony.

question: What did the Discord messages the roommate showed investigators say about retrieving a rifle, engraving bullets and changing outfits?
known: Agent Davis testified Exhibit 16.2 shows the Discord messages Twiggs described (S-5 02:51:08); texts quoted in the Information and ruling refer to a drop point, a towel-wrapped rifle, engraving bullets, a scope and a changed outfit (S-1 pp. 8-9, S-7 07:52:46, S-5 02:46:40, 02:47:11) (C-136, C-137, C-138, C-139).
settle: Settled by the hearing exhibits; the native message export would add timestamps.

question: What was inscribed on the recovered cartridges or casings, who engraved them, and is there any documented link to inscribed casings in other crimes?
known: A text read at the hearing asks 'Remember how I was engraving bullets?' (S-5 02:47:11) (C-138, C-206). The inscriptions themselves are not in the cited record; the host questions them (C-296, C-297), relays a source saying Robinson was bewildered by the idea he carved them (C-952), and calls inscribed casings a possible government signature (C-941).
settle: The evidence log and photographs of the recovered cartridges and casings; forensic tool-mark and handling analysis; investigators' statements on other inscribed-casing cases.

question: Did anyone at the UVU event cheer after Kirk was shot?
known: The host says someone stood up and cheered (C-143). The record says nothing yet.
settle: Crowd video from the event and witness statements.

question: Did anyone within or close to TPUSA act against Kirk in the period before his death, and what records show it?
known: The host says TPUSA employees describe a takeover and that people close to Kirk betrayed him, without naming them (C-482, C-547, C-548, C-549, C-551, C-590). The record says nothing yet.
settle: The documents and names the host says she holds, employee testimony and TPUSA internal communications.

question: What charges does the State bring against Tyler Robinson, what does each count (including Count 6 and the children-present allegation) allege, and does the State seek the death penalty?
known: Robinson faces capital aggravated murder, felony discharge of a firearm, two obstruction counts (rifle, clothing), two witness-tampering counts (delete texts; stay silent) and a violent offense in the presence of a child, and the State seeks death (S-7, S-10, S-11, S-1, S-5). The Information lists Count 6 as witness tampering (telling the roommate not to talk to police), with children present as a separate allegation (S-1 p. 4, S-7 05:01:11); the bindover ruling found children under 14 present (S-7 08:31:41); the overview alleges he hid the gun, discarded clothing and told the roommate to delete texts (S-1 p. 3). The host lists the same charges (C-12606, C-12615, C-12616, C-12617, C-12618, C-12619, C-12621), though her reading of Count 6 differs (C-164).
settle: Settled by the Information, the amended information and the bindover ruling.

question: Where did Robinson dispose of the clothing he wore during the shooting, and has it been recovered?
known: The Information alleges he discarded the clothing and told the family friend he disposed of it in different areas (S-1 pp. 3, 7), and the ruling found he said he had discarded those items (S-7 07:55:06). The host relays a source saying clothes were dropped in a cemetery near a Dairy Queen (C-407, C-576). The location is not in the record.
settle: Search warrants, evidence logs for any recovered clothing, and camera footage from the alleged disposal sites.

question: Which officer first recognised the shot as a rifle shot from the rooftops, and what did he do?
known: The Information says an officer judged from the sound that it was a rifle and looked for sniper positions (S-1 p. 4), and Officer Bagley testified he realised it was a rifle shot (S-2 01:40:24) (C-165).
settle: Settled by the testimony; body-camera footage would add timing.

question: What did Robinson tell his parents before and after the shooting, did he confess to them, and did they give statements supporting the prosecution?
known: The Information alleges he told his mother he was home sick on September 10, called UVU a 'stupid venue', implied to his parents that he was the shooter and said Kirk spreads too much hate (S-1 pp. 6-7) (C-180, C-183, C-185, C-186). These are charging allegations; the parents' interviews and any written statements are not in the cited record. The host says no evidence shows the parents turned him in or that he confessed to them, and that his father believes him innocent (C-12316, C-12320, C-12640, C-12641, C-12653, C-12656).
settle: The probable-cause statement; the parents' recorded interviews and police reports; any written parental statements in the court record; phone records for September 10-11.

question: Was Lance Twiggs detained or questioned after the shooting (reportedly on 2025-09-11), for how long, when was he released, and why was he not charged?
known: The host relays people close to the case and Twiggs's family saying he was taken in on 2025-09-11 around 11:00 p.m. (C-192, C-215, C-222, C-422) and held only a couple of hours without being properly questioned (C-8081, C-8486). The record contains his recorded statement (S-5 Exhibit 16) and a September 11 text to him (S-7 08:28:42) but not his custody status.
settle: Utah and Washington County booking and release records, FBI and Utah County interview reports (302s), search-warrant returns for the residence, and prosecutors' charging statements.

question: What did the note photographed under the keyboard say, who wrote it and when, who photographed it, and is the original in evidence with a chain of custody?
known: The Information quotes it as 'I had the opportunity to take out Charlie Kirk and I'm going to take it' and says police found a photograph of it (S-1 pp. 7-8) (C-195, C-196). The host says Robinson's partner photographed it and the note has 'since been disappeared' (C-597). Authorship, date and chain of custody are not established in the cited record.
settle: The photograph with metadata and the device it was on; the prosecution's evidence list and chain-of-custody records for the note; testimony on its seizure; any forensic handwriting examination.

question: What did Robinson's messages to Lance Twiggs on 2025-09-10 and 09-11 say, including any confession, when was each sent, and are they authentic?

The host says influencers now claim only a confession to Twiggs and calls that false (C-12655). She recites the letter-under-the-keyboard message (C-4522), puts the first exchange after 6:00 p.m. (C-4529), refers to texting right after the shooting (C-4517), and says the messages lack timestamps, conflict with the Panguitch receipt and read like translation (C-10626, C-10627, C-10630, C-10631). The cited record gives no per-message send times or phone locations.
settle: Content: settled by the charging document and hearing exhibits. Timing and authenticity: the forensic extraction report and native message database with time fields, and carrier location records for both phones.

question: At what times were Robinson's texts to Twiggs sent?

question: Whose rifle was used, what is its make and serial number, how did Robinson come to have it, and what was his firearms background?

question: Are the quoted Robinson-Twiggs messages complete and authentic, and were any portions omitted?

question: Is the Dairy Queen photo said to show Robinson authentic, who is in it, and when was it taken (is the 6:38 p.m. time accurate)?
known: The host says the photo spread widely from an unofficial source her outlet used, shows half of each official outfit, and that the 6:38 p.m. time was read off a screen grab (C-402, C-404, C-406, C-13455, C-13456); she discusses poster dating and camera retention (C-574, C-575) and asks why information about the Dairy Queen was withheld and whether the store is under watch (C-949, C-950, C-968). She says the official account has a calm Dairy Queen stop (C-4517) but that the stop must be earlier, perhaps 5:38 p.m. (C-4526, C-4530), that the Panguitch receipt shows 6:38 must be wrong, and offers clock drift or a lookalike as explanations (C-13457, C-13458, C-13464). The record says nothing yet.

question: Who removed the event cameras and SD cards after the shot (including the camera behind Kirk), when and in what order, on whose instruction and why, and what is the cards' chain of custody?
known: The host says a TPUSA-linked man she knows, whom she identifies as AV staffer Terryl Farnsworth (the man in the background of the staff call), sat to Kirk's left, took down the cameras to give footage to the FBI, consulted TPUSA lawyers and showed her the footage over FaceTime (C-502, C-504, C-506, C-508, C-509, C-510, C-513, C-514, C-515, C-591, C-5725). On timing, the host says the rear camera came down first, about four minutes after the shot and about three minutes after the yellow camera fell, after Farnsworth recorded himself announcing Kirk's death, while he stood on Kirk's chair looking around (C-1127, C-1355, C-1643, C-1770, C-2366, C-7686, C-7848, C-12210, C-12211, C-12239, C-12240, C-12284, C-12297); she says footage of the quick removal fuels suspicion (C-867). Kolvet says the team grabbed the SD cards (plural) so law enforcement could get them, that they are with the FBI, that Farnsworth is a long-time friend, and that he took them because people can be evil (C-712, C-1357, C-12229, C-12231, C-12232, C-12292); the host says footage shows only the rear camera's card taken, after which he texted rather than collecting the others (C-12238, C-12244, C-12582). On instruction, Tyler Bowyer first said police ordered the takedown (C-1367); the host calls that a lie, says Farnsworth told her no police officer instructed him, rejects Kolvet's hat-theft and item-protection explanations, and says Farnsworth told her he wanted to keep Erika from seeing the footage (C-1644, C-1761, C-2662, C-2663, C-3994, C-3995, C-7688, C-7690, C-12245). No record yet.
settle: Original time-coded footage of all camera positions after the shot; Farnsworth's, Kolvet's and Bowyer's statements to investigators; police and FBI records of any instruction; evidence logs and chain of custody for each card.

question: Where did the bullet enter Charlie Kirk's body, what path did it take, did it exit, and where in his body was it or its fragments recovered?
known: The bindover ruling finds a neck wound with a front-to-back, slightly left-to-right, downward path, no exit wound, and the bullet coming to rest in the tissues of Kirk's upper back (S-7 07:46:29, 08:16:02; C-7027 corroborated), and fragments were recovered at autopsy (S-5). The host says the bullet entered the front left lower neck and the shot did not come from behind (C-1661, C-1704); she earlier relayed experts calling the front wound an exit wound (C-511, C-518) and argued with a clip guest (Range Day Bro) about blood, a rear entry and an exit (C-592, C-907, C-908, C-910). Accounts of where it was found shifted: Kolvet said the coroner found it just beneath the skin (C-595, C-691, C-1613), and later told the host it travelled from C2 to C6 into the thorax, with other versions naming the stomach (C-7707, C-7708, C-7939). The host says the videos show little blood and no exit, inconsistent with a .30-06, disputes the 'strong bones', 'steel neck' and ricochet explanations offered by Erika Kirk, Kolvet and others (C-3785, C-3978, C-3979, C-3980, C-3988, C-4079, C-4538, C-4571, C-4572, C-6236, C-6237, C-6435, C-6437, C-6755, C-6756, C-7032), and speculates the non-exit was meant to stay secret (C-607, C-7692).
settle: Settled in outline by the ruling; the medical examiner's autopsy report, the trauma surgeon's operative notes and the projectile recovery record with chain of custody would add detail.

question: Did investigators search for a bullet after the shooting, and was a projectile recovered from Kirk's body?
known: The host recalls officials saying they were looking for a bullet (C-517, C-518). The ruling finds the bullet did not exit (S-7 08:16:02), but recovery is not addressed in the cited record.
settle: FBI and Utah briefing transcripts from 2025-09-10 to 09-12, the autopsy report and the FBI laboratory report.

known: The host says the house next door was vacant and owned by UVU (C-602) and that the owner of Caldera Engineering owned houses on the block where employees live (C-661). The record says nothing yet.

question: Which rifle was recovered, and what forensic evidence (ballistics, cartridge case, fingerprints, DNA) links it to Tyler Robinson and to the fatal shot, including whether it was fired on 2025-09-10?
known: Sgt. Faumuina testified the recovered gun was a Mauser 98 rifle (S-3 05:03:26), and the bindover ruling treats a Mauser .30-06 as the suspected murder weapon (S-7). The ATF report identifies the cartridge case found in the rifle as fired in that rifle (S-5); it does not by itself date the firing. Neff and Kolvet say the rifle came from Robinson's grandfather and bore his DNA (C-7396). The host accepts the rifle was Robinson's heirloom but says it was not fired that day or used to kill Kirk and asks for proof (C-7403, C-7674, C-7711, C-7713, C-7894, C-8343, C-10612), says no evidence connecting it to the crime scene was shown (C-11758), says authorities admitted multiple sets of prints on it (C-6234), and questions the comparison methods; defense counsel says the ATF and FBI examined different objects under different protocols (C-8352, C-8388). She thinks the search was for a different weapon (C-649) and relays a roof witness saying the gun he saw was smaller than the recovered rifle (C-688, C-748); Lyman doubts it was ever on the roof (C-1023). No fingerprint or DNA report is in the cited record.
settle: ATF and FBI firearm and toolmark reports with bench notes; ballistic comparison of the projectile and jacket fragment with the rifle; bore, chamber and residue findings; crime-lab latent-print and DNA reports; recovery-time and chain-of-custody records; roof witnesses' recorded statements; trial exhibits.

question: Did someone call Erika Kirk after the shooting to ask how much she knew, as attributed to Andrew Kolvet, and who?

The host names Kolvet and two others as her sources for the offer (C-4498, C-4499, C-4500, C-4545, C-4546, C-5694, C-6275, C-6397, C-6442); Kolvet called a $150 million figure made up, which the host says she never used (C-4113, C-4116).
